title: WPMS/1863/2017 of Ramesh Kumar Vs Sanjay Agarwal

paras.text:
MCC No. 1124 of 2019 (Recall Application)
CLMA No. 15410 of 2019 (Delay Condonation Appl.)
In
WPMS No.1863 of 2017
Honíble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
Mr. Avidit Noliyal, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. Nikhil Singhal, Advocate for the
respondent.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 1863 of 2017 was
filed by Mr. Ramesh Kumar against the
judgment & order dated 29.11.2014 passed by
Prescribed Authority in proceedings under
Section 21 (1) (a) of U.P. Urban Buildings
(Regulation of Letting, Rent & Eviction) Act,
1972 for release of the shop and also against
the judgment & order dated 25.07.2017 passed
by learned Ist Additional District Judge,
Haridwar in Rent Control Appeal No. 78 of
2014. The said writ petition was disposed of
by a Co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order
dated 14.09.2017 in view of the statement
made on behalf of the tenant/petitioner that he
is ready to handover the vacant and peaceful
possession of the premises in question to the
landlord provided some reasonable time is
given to him for the purpose. Operative
portion of the said order is extracted below:
ì3) Although learned counsel for the respondent
opposed the same, but considering the nature of
dispute between the parties, the tenant-petitioner is granted time upto 13.09.2019 to
handover peaceful possession of the premises in
question to the respondent-landlord subject to
the petitioner giving an undertaking within one
month from today before the Prescribed
Authority to the following effect:
(1) The petitioner shall file an undertaking
before the trial court on or before
13.10.2017 that he shall vacate the
premises in question on or before
13.09.2019 and handover vacant and

peaceful possession of the premises in
question to the landlord.
(2) The petitioner should undertake to
deposit the entire decretal amount before
the trial court within a period of two
months from today subject to adjustment
of any amount already deposited before
the court below.
(3) The petitioner should continue to pay
the rent for the use and occupation of the
premises in question on each succeeding
month till vacation of the accommodation
on 7th day of each month.
(4) The petitioner shall not induct any
other person in the premises in question.
(5) In the event of default of any of the
aforesaid conditions, the petitioner shall
not be entitled to continue in the premises
in question up to 13.09.2019 and the
decree shall be executed forthwith.
4) With the aforesaid conditions, present writ
petition is finally disposed of. No order as to
costs.î
 Before the time of two years granted by
this Court could expire, Mr. Ramesh Kumar
(tenant) moved an application seeking
extension of time for vacating the premises in
question. This Court vide order dated
22.08.2019 extended the time for vacating the
premises in question upto 31.10.2019. Mr.
Ramesh Kumar challenged the order dated
22.08.2019, whereby the time for vacating the
premises was extended upto 31.10.2019, by
filing Special Leave to Appeal (C) No.26456 of
2019, which was dismissed by Honíble
Supreme Court vide order dated 14.11.2019.
Now, Mrs. Laxmi Sukhija, who claims to
be the sister of Mr. Ramesh Kumar, has filed
an application seeking recall of final order
dated 14.09.2017. Since, there is delay of 670
days in filing the recall application, therefore,
an application seeking condonation of delay is
also moved.

Reasons furnished in the delay
condonation application are sufficient to
condone the delay in filing the recall
application. Consequently, the delay
condonation application is allowed and the
delay in filing the recall application is
condoned.
After hearing learned counsel for the
parties, this Court does not find any reason to
recall the order dated 14.09.2017. The
applicant was not a party to the release
application, which was filed before the
Prescribed Authority in the year 2012.
Furthermore, Mrs. Laxmi Sukhija never moved
any application seeking her impleadment
before the Prescribed Authority or before the
Appellate Authority or even before this Court in
the proceedings under Article 227 of
Constitution of India.
In such view of the matter, the
application filed by Mrs. Laxmi Sukhija seeking
recall of the final order dated 14.09.2017 is
misconceived.
Accordingly, recall application is rejected.
No order as to costs.
The Executing Court will be at liberty to
proceed further in accordance with law.
